compiled_state.description:
## Why

Surfaced by the plan-v4 divergence-grading calibration (story doggish-nonorganic-tsetsefly), from
the same plan-v3 sidecar corpus (18,085 verified findings).

`undecomposed` fires on **12 of 18,085 findings (0.07%)** — two orders of magnitude below every
other axis — while holding full HARD-OVERRIDE power (any non-none grade floors impact at 0.85 and
auto-blocks). Comparison across the seven axes on plan-v3:

| axis | non-none |
|---|---|
| vague_directive | 31.03% |
| ac_unverifiable | 15.79% |
| internal_conflict | 10.17% |
| divergent_implementation | 7.72% (fixed in plan-v4) |
| dod_uncertifiable | 5.36% |
| irreversible_without_rationale | 1.97% |
| **undecomposed** | **0.07%** |

Two candidate explanations, both worth confirming before touching anything:

1. **Working as intended / correctly suppressed.** The axis's own prompt text says a deterministic
   signal (G5) already suppresses false 'flat plan' findings on tickets that HAVE children, and
   most reviewed tickets do have children. If so, 0.07% is the correct residual and the axis
   simply has a narrow true population — no change needed, just documentation.
2. **Mis-specified / unreachable.** The grading instruction may be so hedged ('Grade ONLY a
   genuine gap') that verifiers never assign it, in which case a real class of flat-plan defects
   is scoring 0.0 the same way the divergence class did before plan-v4.

## What

Investigate, do not pre-commit to a fix:

- Pull the 12 firing findings from the corpus and read them — are they genuine flat-plan defects,
  and did they block?
- Determine how often the G5 deterministic suppressor fires, to separate 'correctly suppressed'
  from 'never assigned'.
- Look for the inverse population: findings whose TEXT describes an undecomposed/flat plan but
  which scored the axis `none` (the same ~90%-missed analysis that motivated plan-v4's
  divergence grading).
- Only if (2) is confirmed, propose a change — and note that any impact-model shape change costs
  an IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump that closes the plan-v4 cohort, so batch it per ADR 0054 §4.

## Testing / Verification

This is an analysis ticket: the deliverable is a recorded finding, so verification is
read-only replay over the persisted sidecar corpus plus source reads. No code changes, no new
eval suite, no bulk re-review sweep (ADR 0054 §4).

- Locate the corpus and count its records with an asserting command, e.g.
  `test -n "$(find .rebar -name '*sidecar*' -o -name '*.jsonl')" && echo CORPUS_PRESENT || echo CORPUS_ABSENT`,
  then a `python3 -c` record count over whatever sidecar/journal path is found. If no corpus is
  reachable from this checkout, that absence is itself recorded as a limit and the analysis is
  scoped to source-level evidence.
- Read the axis definition and the G5 suppressor at source:
  `rg -n 'undecomposed|G5' src/rebar/llm/` — the root must be `src/rebar/llm/`, not
  `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/`, because `decide.py` and `verify_models.py` live under the
  sibling `src/rebar/llm/review_kernel/`. Files to read: `plan_review/det_floor.py`,
  `plan_review/det_lint.py`, `plan_review/pass1.py`, `review_kernel/decide.py`,
  `review_kernel/verify_models.py`, and the two reviewer prompts.
- Distinguish the TWO separate 'undecomposed' mechanisms before measuring anything: (a) the
  PASS-1 finder-side deterministic veto `veto_undecomposed_g5` (`plan_review/det_lint.py`,
  invoked from `plan_review/pass1.py`), which suppresses G5-criterion FINDER findings on tickets
  that have children; and (b) the review_kernel VERIFIER severity axis `undecomposed`
  (`review_kernel/verify_models.py`) whose non-none grade is floored to 0.85 in
  `review_kernel/decide.py`. The 12/18,085 statistic is about (b). If the sidecar corpus does not
  co-record a per-finding G5/has-children signal alongside the verifier axis grade, record that
  as a limit rather than reporting a suppression rate for a mechanism that does not gate the axis.
- Replay the corpus (or the reachable substitute) with a read-only `python3` script that
  tabulates: per-finding `undecomposed` grades, the G5/has-children signal state where recorded,
  and the text-match inverse population. Zero LLM calls.
- Inverse-population match rule (stated, not deferred): case-insensitive regex over each
  finding's `finding` / `evidence` / `suggested_fix` text for
  `undecomposed|flat plan|monolith|not decomposed|no subtasks|no children|single (giant |large )?step|should be (split|broken|decomposed)`;
  report the count of matching findings whose `undecomposed` axis grade is `none`.
- Checked by inspection: the resulting comment on this ticket contains the three readouts named
  in the acceptance criteria below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A comment on this ticket reports the 12 firing findings (criteria, decision, whether the
      floor was load-bearing) and the measured G5 suppression rate — or, if the corpus is not
      reachable from this checkout, states that plainly and reports the equivalent readout from
      the evidence that IS reachable. Verified: run `rebar show f391-5a20-4593-4405 --no-pull`
      and confirm the comment exists and cites per-finding ids (or names the missing corpus).
- [ ] The comment states which explanation the evidence supports (correct-residual vs
      mis-specified) with the counts backing it, and either (a) records 'no change needed' with the
      rationale, or (b) links a follow-up story scoped to the fix. Verified: checked by reading the
      comment in `rebar show f391-5a20-4593-4405 --no-pull` — exactly one of the two outcomes is
      explicitly recorded.
- [ ] A comment reports the inverse population: the count of findings whose text matches the
      flat/undecomposed regex stated in Testing but whose `undecomposed` axis grade is `none`,
      together with the match rule used and a sample of matched finding ids — or, if the corpus is
      unreachable, an explicit statement of that with the substitute evidence used. Verified:
      checked by reading the comment in `rebar show f391-5a20-4593-4405 --no-pull` for a stated
      count (or explicit unreachable statement) and the match rule.
- [ ] Method is ADR-0054-compliant: driven off the persisted sidecar corpus at zero marginal LLM
      cost — no purpose-built eval suite and no bulk re-review sweep. Verified: checked by reading
      the comment's Method section, which names the corpus path + replay script as its instrument,
      and by confirming `git status --porcelain src/ tests/` is clean (no code or eval-suite
      changes were made for this ticket).

## Notes

Analysis-only ticket; it may legitimately close with 'the axis is fine, here is why'.
